claims.text: The component material is prone to hot cracking during fusion welding because of its microstructure.
The component has sustained localized damage.
Friction stir repair uses controlled frictional heating and stirring to form a solid-state bond without melting the material.
Tool rotational and traverse speeds can be controlled to generate adequate frictional heat while remaining below the material's melting temperature.
Friction stir repair will produce a fine-grained repair-zone microstructure.
Friction stir repair will minimize brittle-phase formation in the repair zone.
Lower process temperatures and reduced thermal gradients cause the proposed fine-grained microstructure and minimized brittle-phase formation.
Avoiding formation of a liquefied zone removes the thermal conditions that promote hot cracking.
The thermomechanical action of friction stir repair refines the grain structure.
Grain refinement and formation of a sound joint improve the repair's ability to withstand operating stresses.
Friction stir repair will eliminate the hot-cracking problems observed with traditional fusion-welding repair.
The friction stir-repaired component will remain mechanically durable under elevated service temperatures and high cyclic loads.
Friction stir-repaired components will exhibit fewer hot cracks than fusion-welded components.
Friction stir-repaired components will have greater strength than fusion-welded components.
Friction stir-repaired components will have longer fatigue life than fusion-welded components.
Conventional fusion-welded repairs are prone to hot cracking.
Conventional fusion-welded repairs have inferior mechanical performance under aggressive operating conditions.
The hypothesis is limited to repairs whose process parameters avoid melting while producing sufficient plastic deformation.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis and mechanism claim that hot cracking is eliminated, whereas the predicted outcome and falsification criterion require only a notable or statistically significant reduction in hot cracking.
